newsitem.title: JAPAN: Accounting changes boosted Nomura Q1 profits.
newsitem.headline: Accounting changes boosted Nomura Q1 profits.

text.p: A change in accounting procedures relating to trading activities helped boost Nomura Securities Co Ltd's profits in the first quarter of the 1997/98 business year, Takamichi Arata, a Nomura director, told reporters on Thursday.

He added that, at the end of March 1997, Nomura had unrealised profits of 17 billion yen on trading activities, and that the entire amount was included in profits reported for the first quarter of this fiscal year, following a change in accounting procedures to a mark-to-market method.

"Seventeen billion yen in unrealised profits from trading as of the end of March was included in our first quarter results, so the actual current profit in the first quarter could have been half the profits of a year earlier," Arata said.
He added that profits in the first quarter of 1997/98 were aided by a sharp cut-back in Nomura's operating expenses.

He said that Nomura believes that its earnings will be affected by penalties expected to be imposed by the Finance Ministry as a result of Nomura's involvement in a scandal over payoffs to racketeers.
He added, however, that Nomura wants to post profits in the first half of 1997/98. He did not comment on the specifics of possible administrative penalties by the Finance Ministry.
